etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English grynden, from Old English grindan, from Proto-West Germanic *grindan, from Proto-Germanic *grindaną.

Cognate with Saterland Frisian gríende, griene (“to grind, mill”), Dutch grinden (“to grind”, rare) and grind (“gravel, shingle”), Albanian grind (“to brawl, fight”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To reduce to smaller pieces by crushing with lateral motion.
(transitive) To shape with the force of friction.
(metalworking) To remove material by rubbing with an abrasive surface.
(intransitive) To become ground, pulverized, or polished by friction.
To move with much difficulty or friction; to grate.
(sports, intransitive) To slide the flat portion of a skateboard or snowboard across an obstacle such as a railing.
(transitive) To oppress, hold down or weaken.
(slang, intransitive) To rotate the hips erotically.

quote.citation: 1984, Prince (lyrics and music), “Darling Nikki”, in Purple Rain, performed by Prince and the Revolution:
quote.text: She said, "How'd you like to waste some time?" / And I could not resist when I saw little Nikki grind

definitions.definition: (slang) To dance in a sexually suggestive way with both partners in very close proximity, often pressed against each other.
(slang) To rub one's body against another's in a sexual way; to frottage.

quote.citation: 2013 February 26, Elizabeth Hoyt, Lord of Darkness: Number 5 in series, Hachette UK, →ISBN:
quote.text: She wanted to grind herself against him, wanted to moan, loud and free, wanted to take his hand and make him touch her more firmly.

quote.citation: 2016 August 16, Heather McGovern, A Moment of Bliss, Lyrical Press, →ISBN:
quote.text: He ground against her until he was muttering curses, his kiss rougher than before.

quote.citation: 2017 December 17, Becca Fanning, Shifter Royal Dynasty Vol 1 (Royal BBW Bear Shifter Secret Baby Romance Series), Gizmo Media:
quote.text: She kept grinding until they were both spent: their bliss washing over them entirely.

quote.citation: 2020 April 7, Laurelin Paige, Claire Contreras, Sierra Simone, Skye Warren, Annika Martin, Need You Now, Top Shelf Romance LLC:
quote.text: This morning, we woke up and made out for a solid forty-five minutes, grinding like teenagers until she came against my thigh.

definitions.definition: (video games) To repeat a task a large number of times in a row to achieve a specific goal.

quote.citation: 2013, Will Luton, Free-to-Play: Making Money From Games You Give Away, New Riders, →ISBN, page 38:
quote.text: Similarly, nearly all massively multiplayer online role-playing games (MMORPGs), such as Dungeons & Dragons Online, feature grind: Players repeat tasks, or often “quests”, to gain in-game currency to spend on weapons or other ancillary items.

quote.citation: 2015 February 14, Steven Strom, “Evolve Review: Middle of the food chain”, in Ars Technica‎[1]:
quote.text: To extend the variety past that, you'll need to unlock new units in each class, meaning you have to grind through the rather lengthy process of using every one of your class’ weapons and skills significantly across several matches.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To operate by turning a crank.
To produce mechanically and repetitively as if by turning a crank.
(computing, dated) To automatically format and indent code.
(slang, Hawaii) To eat.
To instill through repetitive teaching.
(intransitive, slang) To work or study hard; to hustle or drudge.

quote.citation: 1862, Frederic W. Farrar, St. Winifred's: or the World of School:
quote.text: One evening, during evening work, Charlie was trying hard to do the verses which had been set to his form.  […]  Wilton, whose conduct had been more impertinent than that of any one else, said to Charlie— “I say, young Evson, how you are grinding.” “I have these verses to do,” said Charlie simply.

definitions.definition: (transitive, slang) To annoy or irritate (a person); to grind one's gears.

quote.citation: 2003, Steven Wunderink, Minding Your Spiritual Business: Life Stories with Life Sense, page 139:
quote.text: I need to pontificate on something that really grinds me. So here goes. I am sick and tired of lazy thinkers using the defense of “legislated morality.”

definitions.definition: The act of reducing to powder, or of sharpening, by friction.
Something that has been reduced to powder, something that has been ground.
A specific degree of pulverization of coffee beans.
A tedious and laborious task.

quote.citation: 1961 February, D. Bertram, “The lines to Wetherby and their traffic”, in Trains Illustrated, page 101:
quote.text: Running again in more open agricultural country, the Harrogate line encounters a short downgrade before the stiff uphill grind to Harrogate begins.

definitions.definition: A grinding trick on a skateboard or snowboard.
(archaic, slang) One who studies hard.

quote.citation: 1900, “Gifford Arthur Nelson”, in The Naughty-Naughtian, page 118:
quote.text: If you are at all bright, don't be a grind. Grinding may make a second-hand genius of you (for all the real things are dead), and if you become a genius you will be sure to smoke dope or swallow laudanum. They all did it.
[…]  I suppose I don't know much about books, compared with you—”“Oh, I was never much of a grind,” the other cut in hastily.

definitions.definition: (uncountable, music) Clipping of grindcore (“subgenre of heavy metal”).
(uncountable, slang) Hustle; hard work.

quote.citation: 2023 September 20, Lucy Ford, “How pop-music's hustle culture anthem was made redundant”, in GQ‎[2]:
quote.text: Everyone has to work, they mourned, and that takes its toll. They weren't glamourising the grind because they knew their effort didn't match the supposed rewards.

definitions.definition: A traditional communal pilot whale hunt in the Faroe Islands.
